Which law governs renting a house in Oklahoma?

The Oklahoma Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, found at 41 O.S. 101 and following, sets the main rules for residential rentals. It dates from 1978, and section 135 directs courts to read it liberally so its purposes are carried out.

Older sections of Title 41, such as the ones on tenancy periods and notices to quit, sit alongside it. A landlord selling a rented house has to read both, because together they cover deposits, repairs, entry and what a sale does to the tenant's rights.

The state has 77 counties and about 3.96 million residents as of 2020. Oklahoma County holds 822,125 of them and Tulsa County 698,782, so many rental sales run through those two county courts.

Deposits

Oklahoma wants deposit money parked in an escrow account with a federally insured institution inside the state. Under 41 O.S. 115(A), misappropriating it is unlawful and can bring up to six months in county jail and a fine of up to twice the amount taken.

Once the tenancy is over, a landlord who keeps any portion owes the remainder back, with no interest, inside 45 days of termination, handover of possession and the tenant's written demand. An itemized written statement must explain whatever was kept.

  • The tenant needs to make a written demand, even when no refund is expected.
  • Stay silent for six months after move-out and the deposit goes to the landlord.
  • Tenants cannot apply the deposit to their last month's rent without the landlord's agreement.

Repairs and what a tenant can do

Under 41 O.S. 118(A) the landlord must keep the unit fit to live in and keep the electrical, plumbing, heating, ventilation and air conditioning that the landlord supplies in working order. Some duties do not apply to single-family homes, such as common-area upkeep, trash containers and supplying water and heat.

For a single-family house the tenant usually pays for utilities and trash service and cares for the lawn unless the lease says otherwise. In any home, the two sides may agree in a conspicuous separate writing that the tenant will do specified repairs or maintenance.

Tenant remedyWhat the tenant must do
Repair and deductWritten notice, then 14 days; the statute text caps the cost at under $100 (41 O.S. 121(B))
Repair or move outWritten notice that the tenant will leave 30 days after notice if the problem is not fixed in 14 days
Unlivable homeWritten notice and move out right away
Essential services cut offWritten notice, then end the rental, fix and deduct, sue for the difference or move and stop paying for that period

The $100 cap in older statute text may have been replaced with one month's rent, so confirm the current cap before relying on a dollar figure.

When can a landlord enter the house?

Before going in, a landlord has to give at least one day's notice, often described as 24 hours. Emergencies and situations where notice is impracticable are the exceptions, and visits must fall at reasonable times. Section 128 lists the permitted purposes: inspections, necessary or agreed repairs, agreed services, and showing the unit to prospective buyers, lenders, tenants, workers or contractors.

A tenant cannot unreasonably say no, and a landlord who is turned away can ask a court for an injunction or terminate the lease. Section 124 gives the tenant a mirror remedy, plus actual damages, when a landlord enters unlawfully or keeps pressing with repeated demands.

If photos or buyer visits are coming, put the notice in writing and offer a few time windows.

Lockouts and utility shutoffs

Forcing a tenant out by changing locks or shutting off services is not allowed. A landlord who wrongly removes or shuts out a tenant owes damages of up to twice the average monthly rent or twice actual damages, whichever is greater, under 41 O.S. 123. The tenant can recover possession through a court case, or end the rental and get deposits and unearned rent back.

The landlord must first send a summons and let the tenant appear in court before moving them out. If you need the house empty before closing, your choices are a court case or a negotiated move-out.

What notice ends a tenancy?

How much notice applies turns on the kind of tenancy. With no written fixed term, the arrangement is month-to-month, or week-to-week for a roomer or boarder who pays weekly.

  • Month-to-month or at-will: either side gives 30 days in writing (41 O.S. 111).
  • Any shorter period: 7 days in writing.
  • Fixed term: the rental simply ends on its stated date, absent a different agreement.
  • Late rent: 5 days following a written demand (41 O.S. 131).

A tenant who keeps occupying the house after the term without permission can be taken to court for possession and damages. A willful holdover in bad faith can cost up to twice the average monthly rent for every month.

Sale of the rental: what happens to the lease

A sale does not end the lease. Section 119 of Title 41 lets a landlord convey the property with no consent from the tenant, and any rent handed to the seller before written word of the sale reaches the tenant still counts against the buyer.

After written notice, rent goes to the new owner. The seller is freed from duties tied to later events, and the buyer answers for every obligation in the rental agreement. Section 114 adds that successors of landlords and tenants have the same rights, duties and remedies as the people they replace.

Pass the deposit records to the buyer as well. Oklahoma's flood rule also follows the house: if the premises flooded in the past five years and the landlord knew, section 113a requires that to be stated prominently in writing in any written rental agreement, or the tenant can sue for personal property damage from flooding.

Abandoned property and a tenant's death

Two sections cover the awkward cases. When a tenant abandons the unit or is lawfully removed, 41 O.S. 130 lets the landlord dispose of items with no apparent value. For valuable items it requires a certified mail notice, and property left 30 days or more is deemed abandoned.

When a sole occupant dies, 41 O.S. 130.1 lets a landlord store the property and hand it to the contact the tenant named, who signs an inventory. The landlord may discard it only after a mailed request goes unanswered for 30 days after the postmark, and must refund the deposit less lawful deductions to the right person.

An heir who inherits a tenant-occupied house inherits these duties, and probate timing can make them harder to meet.

Selling a rented house in Oklahoma

A buyer who accepts the house with the tenant still living there spares you a forced move-out, since the lease carries over under section 119. If you need the house empty, the road is slower, so sort out early which of these issues you face:

  • Month-to-month tenants who are owed 30 days of notice in writing.
  • A deposit that must be accounted for within 45 days of the tenant's demand.
  • Entry limits when buyers or appraisers want a showing.
  • Repair disputes, for example after storm damage to a roof, that can stall a closing.

One sensible order: read the lease for its term and any repair agreement, send a written entry notice before each showing, record the deposit balance, and tell the tenant in writing once a contract is signed. An as-is cash purchase by someone who intends to keep the lease cuts out the repair work and the showings.

Frequently asked questions

How long does a landlord have to return a security deposit in Oklahoma?

45 days after the tenancy ends, possession is delivered and the tenant makes a written demand. A landlord who keeps part must send an itemized statement under 41 O.S. 115(B), and an unclaimed deposit reverts to the landlord after six months.

How much notice must a landlord give before entering a rented house?

At least one day, except in an emergency or where notice is impracticable. Under 41 O.S. 128 the landlord may enter at reasonable times for inspections, repairs and showing the home to prospective buyers.

Can a tenant withhold rent for repairs in Oklahoma?

Only through the steps the statute allows. A tenant must give written notice, wait 14 days and then may deduct the cost of a qualifying repair, so simply refusing to pay is not safe. A tenant who calls the home unlivable cannot keep living there and refuse rent.

What happens to a tenant's lease if the owner sells the house?

The lease stays in force. The buyer takes over the landlord's obligations under 41 O.S. 119, and the tenant pays rent to the buyer once they have written notice of the sale.

Can a landlord change the locks if rent is late?

No. A landlord who excludes a tenant without a court order can owe up to twice the average monthly rent or twice actual damages, whichever is greater, under 41 O.S. 123.

Notices Oklahoma requires before an eviction filing

The right notice turns on the landlord's reason, and the waiting periods span 5 days up to 30 days. Title 41, the Oklahoma Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, sets them. Title 12, beginning at Section 1148.1, governs the lawsuit that follows.

Send the wrong notice and the landlord typically restarts, losing weeks. If you plan to sell, a tenant who cannot be moved out on time can hold up the closing. The main notices are summarized here.

Notice periods for common eviction grounds
SituationNotice periodOklahoma statute
Unpaid rentFive days from a written demand41 O.S. 131(B)
Lease violation that can be curedLease ends 15 or more days after receipt, unless fixed within 10 days41 O.S. 132(B)
Repairable damage by the tenantTen days after written notice to fix it41 O.S. 132(A)
Month-to-month tenancyWritten notice served 30 or more days before the tenancy ends41 O.S. 111(A)
Tenancy shorter than month-to-monthWritten notice served 7 or more days before the tenancy ends41 O.S. 111(B)
Imminent, irremediable harm or criminal activityNo cure period; eviction may be filed immediately41 O.S. 132(C), (D)

The five-day notice for unpaid rent

Step one is a written demand for the missing rent. The tenant then has five days to come up with it, and if the money never arrives the landlord may terminate the rental agreement (41 O.S. Section 131(B)).

The same demand doubles as a demand for possession, so no separate notice to quit goes out. The landlord can send the demand before or after suing for the rent, and may sue for the rent at any point after it comes due.

Nonpayment is the fastest road to possession in the Act. If you are selling, know that a tenant who pays within the five days shuts that road.

Other lease violations

A written notice identifies the violation. Termination can take effect 15 or more days after the tenant gets it, but a tenant who corrects the problem inside 10 days keeps the lease (41 O.S. Section 132(B)).

  • A problem that can be repaired, replaced or cleaned gives the tenant 10 days from the written notice, or less in an emergency.
  • When the tenant ignores it, the landlord may go in, do the work and charge the actual, reasonable cost as rent.
  • A landlord who makes the repair may not terminate the lease over that violation.
  • A later violation can support immediate termination on written notice.
  • Conduct that threatens imminent and irremediable harm, or criminal activity that endangers others or the property, allows an eviction filing with no cure period.

Section 132 further lists drug-related crime on or near the premises, by the tenant, a household member, a guest or anyone the tenant controls, as grounds for immediate termination.

Ending a month-to-month tenancy

Landlord and tenant alike can end a month-to-month or at-will arrangement with written notice served 30 or more days ahead of the end date (Section 41-111). It is the ordinary path for an owner who just wants the house back.

A fixed-term lease ends on its end date with no notice, unless it was ended early under the Act or by agreement. If the tenant stays on without the landlord's consent, the landlord may sue right away for possession and damages. A willful, bad faith holdover can cost the tenant as much as twice the average monthly rent, prorated by the day. If the landlord agrees to let the tenant stay, a month-to-month tenancy results unless the parties agreed otherwise.

Service has its own order. Hand delivery to the tenant is first. Failing that, the notice can go to a household member over 12 who lives there, or be posted on the unit with a copy mailed by certified mail or through the Firm Mailing Book for Accountable Mail.

Someone living there without a lease

Under Section 41-111(G), the notice rules skip anyone with no rental agreement whose stay the landlord never approved. The landlord can order that person out with no eviction case.

Staying past a reasonable time becomes trespass, with a fine of up to $500. A former tenant who once had permission is a different case, so sort out the facts before picking a path.

What the court case looks like

Once the notice period runs out, the landlord files a forcible entry and detainer action in district court. The clerk prepares the starting affidavit and the summons. A claim small enough for small claims goes on that docket (12 O.S. Section 1148.14).

  • Summons form: a plain-language form developed by the Oklahoma Bar Association, available through the Oklahoma State Courts Network.
  • Hearing date: five or more days after the summons issues, with delivery to the tenant three or more days before the hearing (12 O.S. 1148.16). Section 1148.5 repeats the three-day rule for service.
  • Title disputes: a defendant who files an affidavit about title or a boundary has 10 days after filing to answer (12 O.S. 1148.6).
  • After judgment: a new trial motion must come within three days and does not halt execution. The writ tells the sheriff to remove the defendant and give the plaintiff possession (12 O.S. 1148.10).

The clerk at the district court where the rental sits is the best contact for filing fees, forms and hearing dates.

Eviction timing and a rental sale

A buyer who wants the house vacant is waiting on the notice period and the court calendar. The quickest route in the statutes is a five-day notice and then a hearing at least five days after summons. Month-to-month tenants add a full 30 days before filing.

The Act also limits what a lease can contain. Under 41 O.S. Section 113, a lease cannot make the tenant give up rights under the Act, permit a confession of judgment, require the tenant to pay the landlord's attorney fees, or limit the right to call for emergency help. Such terms cannot be enforced, so do not rely on them to hurry things along.

Before you promise a buyer an empty house, read the lease and ask an Oklahoma attorney how a sale affects it. Owners who would rather not wait on a tenant can ask about an as-is offer.

Records to keep

Start a plain file before any notice goes out: lease, rent ledger, when and how each notice was delivered, and photographs of damage. If the case reaches court, those papers answer most of what the judge asks. A buyer curious about the tenant's history will want them too.

Frequently asked questions

How many days notice does an Oklahoma landlord give for unpaid rent?

Five days, counted from the written demand. A tenant who has not paid by then can be terminated under 41 O.S. Section 131(B), and no separate notice to quit is required.

How much notice ends a month-to-month tenancy?

Thirty days of written notice, given by landlord or tenant, before the tenancy ends (41 O.S. Section 111(A)).

What is the notice for a lease violation?

A written notice saying the lease ends 15 or more days after receipt. Fixing the violation inside 10 days cancels the termination (41 O.S. Section 132(B)).

How soon can an eviction hearing be held?

The earliest date is five days after the summons issues, and the tenant must be served three days before the hearing (12 O.S. Section 1148.16).

Can a landlord remove a tenant without going to court, or sell with a tenant in place?

No tenant with a rental agreement can be removed except by a court writ that the sheriff carries out. You may sell a house with a tenant inside, but the lease and notice rules still bind you. A fixed-term lease runs to its end date, and a month-to-month tenant is owed 30 days written notice.
